# Kif9 Knockdown in Zebrafish Embryos

Kif9 (Kinesin family member 9) is a conventional kinesin motor protein involved in intraflagellar transport (IFT) in cilia. It plays a critical role in transporting cargo along the axonemal microtubules to maintain and elongate cilia.

When Kif9 is knocked down in zebrafish embryos, the cilia are still present but are **shorter** than those in wild-type embryos. This is because without functional Kif9, the anterograde transport of structural components to the ciliary tip is impaired, leading to reduced ciliary elongation.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
